picks.rationale: This drug hits his exact allele, and the phase 1 read in G12D PDAC is ORR 30% with 80% disease control and zero grade 4 or 5 events. That toxicity profile is the part I keep coming back to for a 79-year-old: mostly grade 1-2 nausea and rash, nothing that threatens his organ reserve. Upside is the front-line RASolute 305 slot (NCT07621718), where zoldonrasib rides on top of chemo rather than replacing it, so he gets the targeted hit without losing the chemo backbone basal-like disease still needs. The evidence is single-arm and early, and PFS is not yet mature, but a tolerable allele-matched agent in a treatment-naive man with liver-dominant metastatic PDAC is exactly the kind of bet worth making before his window closes.
primary_concerns: ORR 30% has no published 95% CI and PFS/DoR were not reported in the ASCO GI abstract, so durability is unknown
RASolute 305 randomizes against placebo plus chemo, so enrollment carries a chance of the control arm with no allele-targeted agent

picks.rationale: RASolute 302 posted an OS hazard ratio of 0.40 in the RAS G12 group that contains his G12D, with median OS 13.2 vs 6.7 months and grade 3-plus toxicity actually lower than chemo at 43.6% vs 57.5%. For metastatic PDAC that is a startling survival signal, and the front-line RASolute 303 trial (NCT07491445) lets a treatment-naive patient act on it now. The pan-RAS mechanism also covers any subclonal RAS escape his ctDNA has not yet shown. I rank it second only because the pivotal data sit at second line and the skin and mucosal toxicity, grade 3 rash at 14% and stomatitis at 12%, asks more of a 79-year-old than the cleaner zoldonrasib profile.
primary_concerns: registration efficacy is 2L; the 1L benefit is inferred, not yet read out
grade 3 rash and stomatitis in an older patient can drive dose reductions that erode the very exposure the survival signal depends on

picks.rationale: The strongest single-agent response number in the whole dossier comes from here: 37% ORR and 78% disease control in heavily pretreated G12D PDAC, almost all of whom had two or more prior lines. If a drug pulls that off in late-line disease, the front-line setting should do better, which is the bet DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) is making by stacking it on chemo. Monotherapy GI toxicity ran 50-60% but stayed grade 1-2, and the agent went onto full-dose chemo without cutting dose intensity, which matters for a man who still needs his backbone. It sits at rank 3 rather than higher because the data are a single-sponsor phase 1 abstract with immature PFS, and the grade 3-plus neutropenia near 40% lives in the combination cohort he would actually enter.
primary_concerns: the 37% ORR comes from n=41 in a single phase 1 abstract with no confirmed PFS or DoR
grade 3-plus neutropenia around 40% in the chemo combination is a real hit to marrow reserve at 79

picks.rationale: His ARID1A frameshift opens a second, mechanistically independent shot, and ATR inhibition is the live route now that the EZH2 lead agent tazemetostat was pulled. The synthetic-lethal logic is solid in the lab, and NCT03682289 takes pancreatic tumors stratified by ARID1A status, so it is a real fallback if the KRAS agents fail or he progresses. I am honest that this is the thinnest pick on the board: the phase 2 ORR was 14% across all ARID1A-deficient tumors and the activity clustered in gynecologic histologies, with no PDAC responder shown and entry gated on BAF250a IHC loss that the frameshift alone does not confirm. I keep it on the list because a treatment-naive man deserves a banked second axis, not because the current PDAC signal is strong.
primary_concerns: no pancreatic responder in the clinical ARID1A data; the PDAC signal is pure cross-tumor extrapolation
entry needs BAF250a IHC loss, and only about two-thirds of ARID1A-mutant tumors lose the protein, so he may not even qualify
class ATR-inhibitor cytopenias, anemia in particular, can be limiting in an older patient

notes: I deliberately ranked the allele-matched, low-toxicity zoldonrasib above the bigger daraxonrasib survival number because in a 79-year-old the toxicity ceiling is doing as much work as the effect size. I kept the KRAS-vaccine and TCR axes off the ranking: NT-112 and the C*08:02 TCR-T are HLA-mismatched (he is C*05:01/C*06:02, not C*08:02), and ELI-002 and the Hopkins nivo/ipi vaccine only have adjuvant/MRD data that does not fit unresectable metastatic disease, so neither offers a defensible enrollable upside today. Checkpoint monotherapy stays off entirely given MSS and TMB 8.6; the only credible immunotherapy route here is the KRAS-inhibitor-driven FAS/CD8 reprogramming seen preclinically (PMID 37625401), which is a reason to favor the small molecules, not a standalone pick. ECOG 1 is assumed; if performance status is worse, daraxonrasib's skin/mucosal burden would push it below zoldonrasib more decisively.

picks.rationale: This is the only intervention on the board with randomized phase 3 safety data, and that is what moves it to the top for me. RASolute 302 (n=500) recorded grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 43.6% of the daraxonrasib arm versus 57.5% on chemotherapy, with TRAE-driven discontinuation at just 1.2% against 11.2% for chemo. The toxicity is predictable and dermatologic, mostly grade >=3 rash 14% and stomatitis 12%, both with established management algorithms a treating team can run without exotic supportive care. The registration read sits at second line while this man is treatment-naive, so the safe route in is the front-line RASolute 303 trial (NCT07491445); I rank it first on the strength and breadth of its characterized safety, not on a claim that the 1L benefit is proven.
primary_concerns: the grade >=3 AE distribution comes from the 2L registration trial; a treatment-naive 79-year-old on a longer treatment course has not been characterized at that line
skin and mucosal toxicity in an older patient still drives dose reductions even with a good management algorithm, and exposure loss can erode benefit

picks.rationale: On tolerability alone this is the cleanest agent in the dossier: at 1200 mg/day there were no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events, and the common toxicities were low-grade GI (nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, vomiting 15%, rash 10%), almost all grade 1-2, with ALT/AST elevations rare. For a 79-year-old that profile is reassuring, and the agent matches his exact G12D allele. What holds it at rank 2 rather than rank 1 is the depth of the safety base: this is a single-arm phase 1 of n=40 with no published 95% CI on the 30% ORR and no mature PFS or DoR, so the long-tail toxicity and durability are simply not yet characterized. The front-line RASolute 305 trial (NCT07621718) adds it to a chemotherapy backbone, and combined skin/GI plus chemo myelotoxicity has not been reported as a dedicated combination safety read.
primary_concerns: n=40 single-arm phase 1; no 95% CI on ORR and no mature PFS/DoR, so durability and rarer toxicities are uncharacterized
the RASolute 305 chemotherapy combination has no published dedicated combination-toxicity table, so additive myelosuppression at age 79 is unquantified

picks.rationale: The single-agent response signal is the strongest in the dossier (37% ORR, 78% disease control), and as monotherapy the GI toxicity ran 50-60% but stayed grade 1-2 with rash and stomatitis notably absent, which would be attractive in an older patient. My reservation is the combination he would actually enter: DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) stacks it on mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel, and the phase 1 combination cohort already showed grade >=3 neutropenia around 40%. That is synergistic myelotoxicity in a regimen without a dedicated combination safety characterization, which is exactly the pattern my prior treats as a flag at 79. I rank it third because the favorable monotherapy profile is real but the enrollable front-line construct carries an uncharacterized marrow burden.
primary_concerns: grade >=3 neutropenia ~40% in the chemo-combination cohort is a meaningful marrow hit at 79 and is not characterized in a dedicated combination safety trial
the 37% ORR is a single-sponsor phase 1 abstract (n=41) with immature PFS/DoR, so the efficacy that would justify the combination toxicity is not yet durable evidence

picks.rationale: His ARID1A frameshift gives a mechanistically independent second axis, and NCT03682289 enrolls pancreatic tumors stratified by ARID1A status, so I keep it on the list as a banked option. I rank it last and flag a specific missing safety datum: the phase 2 report did not break out per-term grade >=3 toxicity, so the only number in the toxicity table is zero treatment-related deaths, and the expected ATR-class cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia) are unquantified here. no pancreatic responder in the clinical ARID1A data and entry requires BAF250a IHC loss the frameshift does not establish, so both the safety and efficacy bases are thin

notes: No targeted agent here is FDA-approved, so my usual anchor (a category 1/2A regimen with >=5-year post-marketing safety) is unavailable on the feature axis, and the standard chemotherapy backbones sit out of scope for a feature-targeting ranking. Within that constraint I rank by depth of characterized safety, not effect size: daraxonrasib first because RASolute 302 (n=500) is the only randomized phase 3 toxicity dataset on the board, ahead of the cleaner but n=40 single-arm zoldonrasib. preferences.json::toxicity_vetoes is empty, so I issue no round-1 veto; the INCB161734 chemo-combination neutropenia (~40% grade >=3) and the unreported ceralasertib cytopenias are the safety gaps I will press in round 2 if another persona ranks them above their characterization. On the immunotherapy axis the KRAS vaccines are actually the safest things in the dossier by AE profile (ELI-002: zero grade >=3, no CRS, PMID 40790272), but the data are adjuvant/MRD only and do not fit unresectable metastatic disease, so I do not rank them; the HLA-C*08:02 TCR-T and NT-112 are allele-mismatched (he is C*05:01/C*06:02) and excluded. Checkpoint monotherapy stays off given MSS and TMB 8.6; MMR protein IHC is the validation gate before any dMMR/MSI-H claim, and the somatic MLH1 variant most likely reflects MMR-proficient biology. The ASXL1 plasma frameshift should go to paired blood-cell sequencing for CHIP before anyone treats it as a tumor target. ECOG 1 is assumed; a worse performance status would push the chemo-combination options (INCB161734) further down on additive toxicity grounds.

picks.rationale: This is the one intervention on the board carrying randomized phase 3 evidence, so for my prior it is the only pick that clears the bar without an asterisk. RASolute 302 (n=500) hit its registered OS endpoint: HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53, p=4.6e-11), median OS 13.2 vs 6.7 months, with a concordant PFS and ORR signal rather than a lone surrogate. Two caveats keep my confidence at moderate. The trial reads out at second line and this man is treatment-naive, so the front-line claim rests on RASolute 303 (NCT07491445), which has not reported; and his KRAS G12D sits inside a RAS G12 subgroup (HR 0.40, CI 0.30-0.54) rather than a pre-specified G12D-only analysis, so the allele-specific estimate is borrowed from the stratum, not measured.
primary_concerns: RoB2 open-label design (rated 'Some'): performance and treatment-switch bias are live for PFS/ORR, though OS as a hard endpoint is largely insulated
line extrapolation: registration data are 2L, the patient is 1L, and the 1L benefit (RASolute 303) is unread
the G12D estimate comes from a RAS G12 subgroup, not a pre-specified per-allele analysis

picks.rationale: The allele match is real and the mechanism is sound, but the evidence is a single-arm phase 1 of n=40 reported as an ASCO GI abstract, not a peer-reviewed paper. The headline is ORR 30% with 80% DCR, and the abstract gives neither a 95% CI on that response rate nor mature PFS or DoR, so durability is unmeasured. Response rate without a time-to-event readout is exactly the surrogate I discount, and an uncontrolled n=40 cannot separate drug effect from selection. I rank it second only because RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) is a randomized double-blind phase 3 that could convert this signal into real evidence; today it is a promising abstract, not a result.
primary_concerns: single-arm, no comparator: ORR 30% (n=40) cannot be attributed to drug versus selection
surrogate-only endpoint: no CI on ORR, PFS and DoR not reported, so durability is unknown
abstract-stage reporting (ROBINS-I Moderate); selective-outcome reporting cannot be ruled out until full results publish

picks.rationale: Same evidence class as zoldonrasib and the same problems: a single-sponsor phase 1 abstract, n=41, ORR 37% with 78% DCR, and PFS not reached at roughly 5 months of follow-up, which is too short to call durability either way. The number is the highest single-agent response on the board, but I read a numerically higher ORR across two tiny uncontrolled cohorts as noise-compatible, not as evidence that this agent beats zoldonrasib. The front-line construct he would actually enter is DAWN-303 (NCT07522073), where the inhibitor stacks on chemo and the phase 1 combination cohort already showed grade >=3 neutropenia around 40%, a toxicity signal that is itself uncharacterized in a dedicated combination safety analysis. It sits at rank 3 on evidence grade, not on the response number.
primary_concerns: single-arm phase 1 abstract (n=41), ORR 37% with no CI; cross-cohort ORR comparison to zoldonrasib is not interpretable
PFS not reached at ~5 mo: follow-up too short to support any durability claim
grade >=3 neutropenia ~40% in the chemo combination is not characterized in a dedicated combination safety trial

picks.rationale: This is the weakest evidence on the board for this patient and I rank it last on that basis. The phase 2 (NCT03682289, n=29) reported a confirmed ORR of 14% across all ARID1A-deficient tumors, and the 31% figure people quote is a gynecologic histology subset, with zero pancreatic responders shown. Reading a post-hoc endometrioid/clear-cell subgroup across to a basal-like PDAC is cross-tumor extrapolation standing in for indication data, and the preclinical ATR-ARID1A work (PMID 27958275) was done in colorectal and ovarian models with no PDAC line tested. Entry also requires BAF250a IHC loss, which his frameshift call does not establish, so this is not even confirmed enrollable; the per-term grade >=3 cytopenias were not broken out in the abstract, leaving the ATR-class anemia burden in a 79-year-old unquantified.
primary_concerns: confirmed ORR 14% (4/29) overall; the 31% signal is a post-hoc gynecologic subgroup with zero PDAC responders
cross-tumor extrapolation: no pancreatic clinical or preclinical responder; PDAC relevance is inferred
entry gated on BAF250a IHC loss the frameshift does not confirm; per-term grade >=3 cytopenias unreported

notes: I did not abstain because one genuine RCT exists here (RASolute 302, n=500, registered OS endpoint hit at p=4.6e-11), which is rare for a feature-targeting dossier. The rest of the ranking is a graded discount: zoldonrasib and incb161734 are uncontrolled n=40/n=41 phase 1 abstracts reporting ORR without mature time-to-event data, and I treat their numerically different response rates as within-noise rather than as evidence one beats the other. ceralasertib is last because its only positive read is a post-hoc gynecologic subgroup with zero PDAC responders, i.e. cross-tumor extrapolation, and entry is not even confirmed without BAF250a IHC. On the immunotherapy axis I rank nothing: ELI-002 (PMID 40790272) and the Hopkins nivo/ipi vaccine (PMID 41667470) report efficacy split by on-treatment immune response, not randomization (ROBINS-I Serious), and both are adjuvant/MRD only, so neither supports a metastatic claim; the C*08:02 TCR-T (PMID 35648703) and NT-112 are allele-mismatched (he is C*05:01/C*06:02). Checkpoint monotherapy stays off on MSS/TMB-8.6 grounds, and the somatic MLH1 call needs MMR protein IHC before any dMMR claim. The ASXL1 plasma frameshift should go to paired blood-cell sequencing for CHIP before anyone treats it as a tumor target. Caveat I will not paper over: the zoldonrasib, incb161734, and ceralasertib reads are conference abstracts and I have not seen the full per-trial bias profiles; my RoB judgments on those three are provisional on full-text publication. ECOG 1 is assumed.

picks.rationale: I have to say it plainly: no agent on the feature axis carries an NCCN category here, because NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 does not yet list any KRAS G12D-directed small molecule. Daraxonrasib is the one closest to that listing. RASolute 302 is a positive randomized phase 3 (OS HR 0.40 in the RAS G12 stratum that includes his G12D), and the drug now holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation in metastatic G12-mutant PDAC, which is the usual precursor to guideline adoption. NCCN v2.2025 recommends clinical-trial participation as the preferred route for an actionable finding like this, so the guideline-aligned slot for a treatment-naive patient is front-line RASolute 303 (NCT07491445), not an off-protocol prescription.

His G12D estimate is borrowed from the RAS G12 stratum (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.54), not a pre-specified per-allele analysis.
No NCCN category applies yet, so I am ranking on proximity-to-guideline, not on an existing endorsement; that distinction matters for how the treating team frames consent.

notes: Concensusite round 1. The honest guideline reality: on the feature-targeting axis, nothing here carries an NCCN category 1 or 2A, because NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 does not yet list any KRAS G12D agent or any ARID1A-directed agent. The chemotherapy backbones that DO carry NCCN category 1 / 2A (mFOLFIRINOX, NALIRIFOX, gem/nab-paclitaxel) are out of scope for a feature ranking. So I rank by proximity-to-guideline: daraxonrasib #1 (only positive randomized phase 3 + FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation, closest to a future listing), the two front-line randomized phase 3 G12D trials next, ceralasertib last (off-indication extrapolation, weakest guideline fit). NCCN v2.2025 recommends comprehensive somatic NGS + germline testing and MSI/MMR testing for all metastatic PDAC, and names clinical-trial participation as the preferred route for actionable findings, which is why every pick is framed as the trial it enters rather than an off-protocol prescription. Immunotherapy is off the ranking on guideline grounds: pembrolizumab is endorsed (NCCN and ESMO) only for dMMR/MSI-H, and this tumor is MSS with TMB 8.6 and germline-negative, so the somatic MLH1 variant most likely reflects MMR-proficient biology; MMR protein IHC is the validation gate before any dMMR/MSI-H claim, and I do not recommend pembrolizumab on that label here. The C*08:02-restricted anti-G12D TCR-T and NT-112 are HLA-mismatched (he is C*05:01/C*06:02), and ELI-002 and the Hopkins nivo/ipi vaccine have adjuvant/MRD data only, which does not fit unresectable metastatic disease. The ASXL1 plasma frameshift should go to paired blood-cell sequencing for CHIP before anyone treats it as a tumor target. ECOG 1 is assumed; performance status was not supplied and is decision-critical at 79, so the willingness to surface trial-only options should be revisited if it is worse. Humanizer pass applied to prose fields; guideline names and versions kept verbatim.

picks.rationale: The preference file gives me almost nothing to weigh against: no toxicity vetoes, no modality constraints, a neutral 0.5 efficacy/toxicity balance. It is the only feature-targeting option here with randomized phase 3 data behind it, and the front-line door is open and recruiting: RASolute 303 (NCT07491445) takes treatment-naive metastatic PDAC and accepts his KRAS G12D under its RAS-mutant criterion. It is oral, which costs the patient nothing under a silent modality field but is worth flagging for a 79-year-old. Pan-RAS covers G12D, so it speaks to the lead driver rather than a side axis. I rank it first because a man who wants a trial can actually get on this one at his line, not because the 1L benefit is settled.

For a 79-year-old that profile matters more than the free_text's neutral 0.5 lets me say outright, and it is the agent that matches his exact G12D allele. prefers_trials is honored too: RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) requires KRAS G12D and is recruiting at first line. With prefers_trials in play it also clears the bar a patient cares about: DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) requires KRAS G12D and enrolls previously untreated metastatic PDAC, and the phase 1 parent (NCT06179160) takes him at first line too. picks.intervention_label: ELI-002 2P, lymph-node-targeted amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine (G12D/G12R)
picks.rationale: I am surfacing the KRAS vaccine deliberately, because the immunotherapy axis here is full of HLA traps and this is the one that does not spring on him. The published anti-KRAS-G12D TCR-T is HLA-C*08:02-restricted and he is C*05:01/C*06:02, so that product cannot present his epitope at all; ELI-002 is HLA-agnostic, so his class I genotype does not exclude it. Its safety is the cleanest thing in the case: no grade 3 or worse treatment-related events across 25 patients, mostly fatigue and injection-site reactions. The honest problem is the setting. The data come from resected, minimal-residual-disease PDAC, and this man has a large primary and liver mets, so the efficacy read does not transfer to bulky metastatic disease. I rank it here, not higher, as a trials-forward option to keep on the table rather than a regimen I would put first.
primary_concerns: clears every HLA gate where the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T fails, and the toxicity is the lowest in the dossier, which suits the patient; but the MRD/adjuvant evidence does not match unresectable metastatic disease

Entry is gated on BAF250a IHC loss, not the frameshift call alone, so he would need that tissue test before any ATR trial would take him. prefers_trials is technically served by the NCT03682289 basket, but it is active-not-recruiting, so the door a trials-leaning patient wants is not currently open here.

notes: The preference file is effectively empty on the axes I normally fight over: toxicity_vetoes [], modality_constraints [], weight a neutral 0.5. So there is no veto to defend and no oral-only line to hold. The single preference carrying weight is prefers_trials=true, and I let it drive the top of the ranking toward agents with open, recruiting front-line PDAC trials (daraxonrasib RASolute 303, zoldonrasib RASolute 305, INCB161734 DAWN-303). I flag the one tension the case author already named in free_text: a neutral 0.5 understates how toxicity-averse a 79-year-old probably is, which would push zoldonrasib's tolerability up and INCB161734's chemo-combination neutropenia down if a real preference were captured. On the immunotherapy axis I am holding the line on the patient's behalf: the C*08:02 TCR-T and the A*11:01/C*08:02 mRNA vaccine are HLA-excluded for him, so I will not let them be surfaced as live options; only the HLA-agnostic ELI-002 vaccine survives the genotype, and even that sits low because its evidence is adjuvant/MRD, not metastatic. Checkpoint monotherapy stays off my list entirely given MSS, TMB 8.6, and the single somatic MLH1 variant that most likely reflects MMR-proficient biology; MMR IHC is the gate before anyone claims the dMMR/MSI-H pembrolizumab label.
